coverage.name: Adams County
limitations: Read the Adams County 2026 coordinated election TABOR notice (50 pages, certified by the Clerk & Recorder, posted 2026-09-24). It contains issues from City of Aurora (3A, 3B, 3C), City of Northglenn (3H), Westminster Public Schools (4A), Bennett School District 29J (5A), North Range Metropolitan District No. 3 (6A-6D), Adams County Fire Protection District (6E), Central Colorado Water Conservancy District (7B), its Groundwater Management Subdistrict (7C), Greater Brighton Fire Protection District (7D), and Bennett Fire Protection District (7F, 7G). None is an Adams County issue; none is housing-related.

The TABOR notice covers only tax/debt/revenue-retention issues, so a non-TABOR county question (for example a land-use or charter-type question) could appear only on the sample ballot. News reports (not official) mentioned a possible District Attorney term-limits referral and a non-binding secession question; the sample ballot check below settles both.

No list of political subdivisions participating in the Adams County Nov 3, 2026 coordinated election is published (the elections page and the 'Information for Coordinating Entities and Candidates' page were checked on 2026-09-26; the latter describes the IGA process only).

Checked 2026-10-12 against the county's all-inclusive sample ballot (posted 2026-09-28): it carries no Adams County ballot issue or question. Its local content is Front Range Passenger Rail District 7A, 17th Judicial District Question 7E (district attorney term limits, a judicial-district question), Thornton 2A (council resignation on candidacy; charter), Aurora 3A-3C and Aurora Question 3D (moving city elections to even-numbered years; governance), Northglenn 3H, Westminster Public Schools 4A, Bennett 29J 5A and the special-district issues 6A-6E, 7B-7D, 7F and 7G. None is housing-related, and no secession question is on the ballot.

coverage.name: Bennett (town)
limitations: Read the Adams County official 2026 General Election sample ballot posted 2026-09-28. It contains Bennett School District No. 29J Issue 5A and Bennett Fire Protection District Issues 7F and 7G, but no Town of Bennett question. Those district questions are not town questions and do not qualify for this municipal row.

Bennett's Town Clerk page (https://www.bennettco.gov/node/106) and 2026 municipal election page (https://www.bennettco.gov/town-board-trustees/page/2026-town-bennett-municipal-election) could not be opened during the 2026-10-04 recheck. Search results refer only to the April election and do not show November coverage. The current town sources remain unreadable, so this row is source_unreadable, not none_found, and needs a further check.

The Adams County elections page and its Information for Coordinating Entities and Candidates page were reviewed on 2026-10-04. The latter describes the IGA process but neither page provided a separate participating-entities list; the official sample ballot was reviewed for all published ballot content.

coverage.name: Northglenn (city)
limitations: Participating: the county TABOR notice contains City of Northglenn Ballot Issue 3H, and the city clerk's elections page states 'City Council has approved the submission of one ballot issue at the Nov. 3, 2026 election'.

Excluded: Ballot Issue 3H (INCREASE IN SALES TAX ON ACCOMMODATIONS SERVICES) raises the accommodations sales tax from 5% to 8% 'WITH PROCEEDS TO BE USED FOR GENERAL GOVERNMENTAL PURPOSES, INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, PUBLIC SAFETY, STREET MAINTENANCE, PARKS, RECREATION, AND CULTURE, AND ADMINISTRATIVE FUNCTIONS OF THE CITY' - a lodging tax not dedicated to housing.
Checked 2026-10-12 against the county's all-inclusive sample ballot (posted 2026-09-28): City of Northglenn Ballot Issue 3H is the only Northglenn measure, matching the city page.

coverage.name: Thornton (city)
limitations: Read the Adams County official 2026 General Election sample ballot posted 2026-09-28. It contains only City of Thornton Ballot Question 2A, a charter amendment concerning when a mayor or councilmember vacates office after declaring candidacy for another office.

Thornton's official Elections & Voter Information page describes the same proposed charter vacancy amendment. The question does not create, extend or earmark housing revenue and does not change land use or housing regulation, so no entry was created.

The Adams County elections page and its Information for Coordinating Entities and Candidates page were reviewed on 2026-10-04. The latter describes the IGA process but neither page provided a separate participating-entities list; Thornton's official page confirms participation in the county coordinated election.
